purpose: The APPROVAL BOUNDARY between the audit layer and production audio. A rendered/spoken form reaches the TTS provider ONLY if it is authorised here. The existence of a renderText in the audit layer authorises nothing.

invariant.identity: de / headword — manifest key, contentHash, assetId, globalId. NEVER changed by an approval.
invariant.synthesis: renderDe || de — the only thing an approval can change.
invariant.failClosed: scripts/promote-renders.js promotes nothing that is not matched by an enabled rule or listed in rows[].

provenanceClasses.A: authoritative recovery — the spoken text already exists verbatim in an authoritative source (the manifest's own `de`, or an authored chapter-data field). No linguistic inference.
provenanceClasses.B: deterministic transformation, explicitly approved rule by rule.
provenanceClasses.C: audit inference — NOT approved. Includes the 230-row gender-suffix-family CSV, which is labelled PROPOSED / AWAITING HUMAN SIGN-OFF and has never been native-speaker verified.
provenanceClasses.D: editorial review — a human decision is outstanding.
provenanceClasses.E: not audio — must never be synthesized.

categoryApprovals.appliesTo: story, listening, reading rows whose audit renderTextSource is 'authored manifest (punctuated)'
categoryApprovals.rule: renderDe := the manifest entry's own `de`, when the UI lookup text differs from it only by dropped punctuation.
categoryApprovals.whySafe: This restores text the manifest ALREADY holds. The UI strips punctuation tokens when building its lookup key; nothing is invented, and the promoted string is byte-identical to the authoritative source.
categoryApprovals.guard: canonical-equivalence: promoted renderDe must reduce to the same letters/digits as the row's lookup text. A mismatch is refused.

categoryApprovals.appliesTo: rows whose audit renderTextSource is 'A · authored chapter-data field'
categoryApprovals.rule: renderDe := the authored chapter-data field (reading.tokens reconstruction incl. punctuation).
categoryApprovals.whySafe: The spoken form is read from authored chapter data, not derived.

categoryApprovals.appliesTo: the 7 rows whose renderTextSource is 'B · token stream reconstruction'
categoryApprovals.note: Deterministic, but reconstructs rather than recovers. Left disabled pending sign-off.
HARD BLOCKED. Rests on unverified morphological judgement.

rowSchema.assetId: stable asset identity (manifest id for sentence rows, globalId for vocabulary)
rowSchema.displayText: REQUIRED for token/word rows. The learner-facing surface, and the MANIFEST KEY the runtime looks up. The engine's resolveInfo() keys on nothing else, so an asset published for the token "Z" must be keyed "Z" — keying it on its spoken form would make the popup unable to find its own audio.
rowSchema.renderDe: exact text to synthesize. For token rows this legitimately DIFFERS from displayText ("Z" is spoken "Zett"); the filename hash is taken over this value, so identical spoken content is content-addressed to one shared file.
rowSchema.approvedOn: ISO date — a null value means NOT approved; scripts/generate-token-audio.ts refuses the row

rowSchemaNotes.identityVsSynthesis: displayText is identity; renderDe is synthesis input. Never the reverse.
rowSchemaNotes.neverTtsInput: a token's `pron` field is a learner-facing respelling ("tset", "vay") written to be READ, never validated as TTS input. It must never be promoted to renderDe.
rowSchemaNotes.tokenRowsPending: the 13 authored token spokenDe values (a1-1/a1-2 Letter+Vowel targets) are NOT listed in rows[] and therefore cannot be synthesized. The 12 REVIEW targets (R C B T W e i o u Ä ts Üüü) have no authored spoken form at all.

hardBlocked.kindsNote: the 1,277 speaking task-prompt rows have no learner-facing audio control and must never be promoted or synthesized.

rowsNote: 13 authored token renders, approved for TTS generation. displayText is the manifest identity; renderDe is the synthesis input. The 12 remaining Letter/Vowel/Sound targets (R C B T W e i o u Ä ts Üüü) have no authored spoken form and are NOT approved.
